title: No total calories ? Come On!
body:
I felt compelled to come to write this  - as a long-time Apple user who tracks activity, training, and nutrition seriously, and I want to express deep frustration with a glaring omission in Apple Health.

With the aid of Apple Watch, Apple Health already calculates and stores both Resting Energy and Active Energy. These values are visible, accurate, and available daily, weekly, and monthly. Yet Apple Health still refuses to show the most basic and meaningful metric derived from them:

Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE)  
(Resting + Active calories)

This is not an advanced or niche feature. It is the fundamental number used by anyone managing body weight, performance, recovery, or nutrition. Every athlete, coach, clinician, and informed user understands energy balance — and Apple Health deliberately withholds the one number that makes the data actionable.

The irony is hard to miss:
- Apple already has the data  
- Apple already displays both components  
- Apple already performs far more complex calculations elsewhere  

Yet users are forced to manually add numbers or rely on third-party apps to see a value that should be obvious and native.

The current design strongly suggests that Apple is prioritizing a simplified, “feel-good” experience over honest, useful physiology. While that may suit casual users, it actively undermines Apple Health’s credibility as a serious health platform.

To be blunt:  
A health app that cannot show total calories burned per day — weekly and monthly — is incomplete.

This omission feels ideological, not technical, and it unnecessarily pushes knowledgeable users out of Apple’s own ecosystem UI while still depending on Apple Watch data behind the scenes.

Please reconsider this decision. A simple, optional “Total Energy” view would dramatically improve Apple Health for users who actually want to understand their bodies, not just close rings.

Right now, Apple Health feels like a data warehouse that refuses to tell you what the data means.

That is disappointing — and entirely fixable.

title: Great potential, but still very immature
body:
The product still feels very immature. It collects an incredible amount of data, but the actual output is surprisingly weak compared to what should be possible. Sometimes it even fails to work at all – for example, during open water swims I can go 200–300 meters and it still shows zero distance.

The overall user experience also needs major improvement. If I want to quickly find a run from a few weeks ago to check my pace or heart rate zone, it’s far too complicated. I often need to search online or ask for help, which really shouldn’t be necessary for something so basic.

I still see a lot of potential here – with this amount of data, the product could be amazing. But right now the UX, reliability, and accessibility of insights need serious attention.

title: Quite a lot of problems with this app
body:
First and foremost, is the sleep recognition from the apple watch: it is simply wrong. If I have my sleep schedule set between 10 pm and 7 am, but lie in bed reading a boon until 11:30 pm, the app writes it down as deep sleep. On the contrary, during the night it fails to recognise any deep sleep I must be having. This is a huge disappointment because the app is useless, if you don’t sleep like a robot. The goal for me was to improve my circadian rhythm, but I just get the wrong kind of data.

Secondly, the layout is horrible. Let’s use the above example and say the app makes a mistake in the time I have gone to sleep. Why do I need to scroll all the way down to manually correct the data? Furthermore, why on earth do I have a menstruation cycle tab as a male in my overview? Why can’t I customise the layout and get rid of the medicine and cycle tabs, for instance?!

Apple, your products get more and mir expensive, but the quality leaves quite a bit to be desired.
